claims.text: Previous efforts produced HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed GNN using multiscale chemical-heterogeneity descriptors will accurately predict Young’s modulus for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed GNN will accurately predict yield strength for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed GNN will accurately predict fracture toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
High-resolution microstructural characterization can provide geometric and chemical-fluctuation descriptors suitable for graph features.
Multiscale chemical heterogeneities mediate the relationship between local bonding and chemical environments and the macroscopic mechanical response.
Incorporating physical constraints and microstructural descriptors into the learning architecture will reduce overfitting.
The GNN can learn interactions across the multiple length scales represented by the hierarchical heterostructure.
Learning cross-scale interactions in one GNN will reduce computational demand relative to scale-separated or solely physics-based simulations.
The proposed method will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 15–20% relative to thermophysical-parameter calculations and conventional machine-learning approaches.
The proposed method will reduce computation time by roughly a factor of ten.
Existing thermophysical-parameter, CALPHAD, first-principles, and conventional machine-learning methods require significant computational resources.
Existing approaches have lower predictive efficiency, particularly for fracture properties.
The model may become unreliable when required high-resolution microstructural descriptors cannot be obtained.
The model may become unreliable for unexpected phases or microstructures substantially outside its training distribution.
The model may become unreliable at temperatures or strain rates substantially outside its training range.
